summary: Validated the new FAST-FINISH auction logic in /app/backend/routers/transfers.py (lines 357-422) on the CM corridor. All 4 backend tests PASS. Auction round finished in 6.60s (server elapsed_sec) well under the 30s cap. round_ended_early WS event is broadcast with reason='all_agents_responded' and valid_bids=2; agent_assigned arrives immediately after. Backward compatibility verified (agent_assigned still emitted, selection picks bid_fee_percent ≤ client_fee_pct). Bid-cap regression on POST /api/agent/auctions/{id}/bid still returns HTTP 400 for over-cap bids.
critical_code_review_comments: transfers.py:443 — `return await _run_fallback(...)` makes the lines 445-468 unreachable (ULTIMATE FALLBACK block is dead code). Recommend removing the duplicate block to avoid confusion.

transfers.py:312 — `random.uniform(2, ROUND_SECONDS - 3)` schedules agent responses in [2s, 27s]. With only 2 agents the average pool finishes around 13-15s, leaving plenty of headroom for fast-finish — good. But when destination has many agents (PER_ROUND=10) the latest scheduled agent will respond ~27s in, so fast-finish saves at most ~3s; consider scaling the schedule window to ROUND_SECONDS or rebalancing if real agents are expected to be faster.

transfers.py:413-422 — In the late-bid arrival branch, `elapsed_sec` is computed as `elapsed + waited` where `elapsed` already excludes the scheduling phase; semantics look correct but worth a comment for future readers.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing seeded CM agents (Patrick Mbarga, Esther Ngassa) and demo client wallet (1250.50 EUR).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file /app/backend/tests/test_auction_fast_finish.py covers fast-finish + bid-cap regression on CM corridor. Connects WS via wss://...EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL/api/ws/auction/{id}?token=...
